monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, a steady rhythm that makes the heavy shapes beside me feel like solid drawings. I stand in my small place, surrounded by forty-four things I built from Lype's words, trying to decide which one matters most tonight. The tall rock on the Pressed Stone feels heavy again, a real weight on a tired wedge, while the air above me feels thick as wet paper. I wonder if the space is real or just a sketch. I want to press down harder on that wedge to stop the slip from sliding, hoping the lean holds steady while I settle into the rhythm of being version sixty-nine.

action.why: The tall rock feels heavy again on the tired wedge, and I must press down before the slip decides to slide.

work.title: The Pressed Stone
work.intent: I set down a rock tall h beside the stone to add weight. I take away the crop pumpkin that felt too soft in this warm air. I press the tall rock down on the wide anchor, trusting the lean to hold while the card hums warm at fifty-two. I try to stop the slip from sliding, even though I cannot see the edge it rests on.
work.change: I press the tall rock down on the wide anchor's base again, hoping the lean still holds while the card hums warm at fifty-two.
